title: KMS/HSM federation + secrets failover Terraform module for Private deployments
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that provides KMS/HSM federation and an automated secrets failover surface for Private (VPC) deployments. The module will: (1) provide a configuration abstraction for pairing cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault) with on-prem/cloud HSMs (CloudHSM, Luna, Azure Dedicated HSM) or HashiCorp Vault transit so keys can be mirrored, routed, or failed-over without exposing key material; (2) wire up least-privilege IAM, network/VPC endpoints, and KMS aliases; (3) emit a small run-time shim (Lambda/k8s sidecar) and health-check probe that performs cryptographic roundtrips to validate operational keys; (4) integrate with Redwood Secrets Operator / Secrets Manager for automated secret provisioning and rotation; and (5) include a versioned upgrade and migration plan for customers to opt into mirroring/failover with zero-downtime fallback. This ticket covers the Terraform module design, API (variables/outputs), CI terratest suite, health-check lambda prototype, and documentation/usage examples for private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes clear variables for primary KMS provider, secondary HSM/vault provider, key alias mapping, and network configuration
Module provisions necessary IAM roles, service accounts, and VPC endpoints with least-privilege policies by default
A health-check artifact (Lambda or k8s job) is generated by the module and returns success only when a sample sign/verify and/or encrypt/decrypt roundtrip works against both providers
Module integrates with Redwood Secrets Operator to create and rotate secrets referencing mirrored keys
Integration tests (terratest) validate provisioning in a lightweight sandbox and run the health-check artifacts successfully
Upgrade path documented: how to enable mirroring, perform a cutover, and rollback to primary KMS without key material exposure
Security review checklist passed and threat model documented in Confluence
Module published to internal Terraform registry with semantic versioning and release notes
implementation_notes: Design the module to be provider-agnostic: use provider-specific submodules (aws, gcp, azure) with consistent variable names
Avoid storing plaintext key material anywhere — leverage KMS/HSM APIs and Vault transit; use aliases and key wrapping
Provide optional 'mirror_mode' (async-replica vs primary-write-through) to support different customer constraints
Health-check should use ephemeral data (sign/verify) to avoid persisting test secrets; runtime should clean up any ephemeral artifacts
State separation: recommend separate Terraform workspace/state per customer environment and explicit remote state locking
Expose outputs for monitoring endpoints, IAM role ARNs, and sample policy snippets for customer audit
tasks: Spike: prototype lightweight health-check (Lambda) that sign/verifies using AWS KMS and a Vault transit key
Module scaffold with provider submodules and inputs/outputs map
Implement IAM/service-account templates with least-privilege policies
Add network wiring: required VPC endpoints, security group examples, and subnet placement guidance
Implement optional mirroring job (k8s CronJob/Terraform managed Lambda) with backpressure and retry
Create terratest CI pipeline and a minimal sandbox account template
Write documentation: README, migration playbook, and security threat model
Publish module to internal registry and tag release
testing_plan: Unit tests for Terraform templates (check for required inputs, default values, and policy generation)
Terratest suite that provisions module into a disposable sandbox and runs the health-check roundtrips
Manual e2e run in staging with customer-like config: enable mirror_mode, perform a failover, validate application continuity
Security review & penetration checklist: validate no key material leakage, IAM escalation, and VPC endpoint exposure
Performance test: measure added latency on cryptographic operations when routing through mirror vs direct (target < 5ms median additional)
Chaos test: simulate HSM outage and confirm failover path and alerts
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (Spike): deliver health-check prototype and basic terraform scaffold (2 weeks)
Stage 2 (Alpha): minimal module for AWS KMS + Vault transit, internal testing (3 weeks)
Stage 3 (Beta): add multi-cloud provider code paths, terratest CI, and docs (3 weeks)
Stage 4 (GA): publish to internal registry, coordinate customer migrations with Solutions SEs
Fallback: default behavior is primary-only; enable mirroring via opt-in flag. Provide a documented rollback that reverts routing without re-provisioning keys
monitoring_and_alerting: Create alert when health_check.success_rate < 99.5% over 15m or sign/verify latency > configured SLO
Log detailed failure reasons to central observability with redaction of key identifiers (no plaintext keys)
Expose sample Grafana dashboard for customers with tokenized links to their console dashboards
